cat__gender1_1.0.label: Needs caution
cat__gender1_1.0.reason: Sex is a structural covariate associated with both sleepiness and many sleep-disorder risks (e.g., OSA prevalence, insomnia patterns). It can confound associations rather than represent a modifiable causal factor.

cat__types5_2.0.label: Needs caution
cat__types5_2.0.reason: This appears to be a categorical self-report sleep/health type variable; without definition it may proxy symptoms, behaviors, or diagnoses related to sleepiness. It could be confounded by underlying health status and sleep disorders.

cat__types5_3.0.label: Needs caution
cat__types5_3.0.reason: Unclear category meaning; it may encode sleep-related phenotype or complaint that correlates with daytime sleepiness. Risk of confounding or partial overlap with the outcome depending on what the category represents.

cat__types5_4.0.label: Needs caution
cat__types5_4.0.reason: Unspecified categorical type may reflect sleep problems, treatment, or comorbidity linked to sleepiness. Interpretation is uncertain and may be confounded by underlying disease severity.

num__REM_pct.label: Plausible
num__REM_pct.reason: REM proportion reflects sleep architecture; altered REM can indicate fragmentation or circadian misalignment that can increase daytime sleepiness. It may also mediate effects of disorders like OSA or depression.

num__extrahrs5.label: Plausible
num__extrahrs5.reason: Extra hours (often napping or extended time in bed) can reflect compensation for insufficient/poor sleep and can influence perceived sleepiness. Directionality can be bidirectional, but a physiological link is plausible.

num__sleepage5c.label: Needs caution
num__sleepage5c.reason: Age is a structural covariate affecting sleep architecture, circadian timing, and comorbidity burden, all related to sleepiness. It is a common confounder rather than a direct modifiable exposure.

num__bmi5c.label: Plausible
num__bmi5c.reason: Higher BMI increases risk of sleep-disordered breathing and hypoxemia, which can cause excessive daytime sleepiness. BMI can also relate to inflammation and cardiometabolic factors affecting fatigue.

num__SWA_Late.label: Plausible
num__SWA_Late.reason: Late-night slow-wave activity reflects homeostatic sleep pressure dissipation and sleep quality. Reduced or abnormal SWA can indicate nonrestorative sleep contributing to daytime sleepiness.

num__pNN50_pct.label: Plausible
num__pNN50_pct.reason: pNN50 is an HRV metric reflecting parasympathetic activity; reduced vagal tone can accompany sleep fragmentation, stress, or OSA. Autonomic dysregulation is plausibly linked to nonrestorative sleep and sleepiness.

num__RMSSD_ms.label: Plausible
num__RMSSD_ms.reason: RMSSD reflects short-term vagal modulation; lower values can indicate sympathetic predominance seen with arousals, hypoxemia, or stress. These processes can impair restorative sleep and increase sleepiness.

num__DesaturationIndex.label: Plausible
num__DesaturationIndex.reason: Frequent oxygen desaturations indicate sleep-disordered breathing severity and intermittent hypoxia. Intermittent hypoxia and related arousals can directly increase daytime sleepiness.

num__MeanRR_ms.label: Plausible
num__MeanRR_ms.reason: Mean RR (inverse of heart rate) reflects autonomic state during sleep; elevated sympathetic tone can signal fragmented sleep or respiratory events. Such disturbances can contribute to daytime sleepiness.

num__MeanSpO2.label: Plausible
num__MeanSpO2.reason: Lower mean nocturnal oxygenation suggests hypoventilation or sleep-disordered breathing. Chronic nocturnal hypoxemia can impair sleep quality and promote daytime sleepiness.

cat__wrksched5_5.0.label: Plausible
cat__wrksched5_5.0.reason: Work schedule categories can capture shift work or irregular hours that disrupt circadian alignment and sleep duration. Circadian misalignment is a well-established cause of excessive sleepiness.

num__MeanHR_bpm.label: Plausible
num__MeanHR_bpm.reason: Higher mean sleep heart rate can reflect sympathetic activation from arousals, hypoxemia, or stress. These factors can reduce sleep restorative value and increase daytime sleepiness.

num__T90_pct.label: Plausible
num__T90_pct.reason: Time spent below 90% oxygen saturation reflects hypoxemic burden during sleep. Greater hypoxemia is linked to neurocognitive impairment and excessive daytime sleepiness.

num__HypopneaIndex.label: Plausible
num__HypopneaIndex.reason: Hypopneas contribute to sleep fragmentation and intermittent hypoxia. Both mechanisms can increase daytime sleepiness.

cat__wrksched5_3.0.label: Plausible
cat__wrksched5_3.0.reason: Work schedule categories can indicate circadian disruption and sleep restriction. These are direct physiological drivers of sleepiness.

num__TST_min.label: Plausible
num__TST_min.reason: Total sleep time is a primary determinant of homeostatic sleep pressure. Shorter TST increases daytime sleepiness through sleep debt.

cat__race1c_2.0.label: Needs caution
cat__race1c_2.0.reason: Race is a structural/social covariate that can proxy socioeconomic factors, healthcare access, and environmental exposures affecting sleep and sleepiness. It is not a direct physiological cause and is prone to confounding.

cat__race1c_3.0.label: Needs caution
cat__race1c_3.0.reason: Race categories often capture social determinants correlated with sleep disorders and reporting differences. Associations with sleepiness are likely confounded by structural factors.

cat__race1c_4.0.label: Needs caution
cat__race1c_4.0.reason: Race is a proxy for structural and environmental determinants that influence sleep health. Treat as a confounder/stratifier rather than a causal exposure.

cat__smkstat5_1.0.label: Plausible
cat__smkstat5_1.0.reason: Smoking can worsen upper-airway inflammation, sleep quality, and cardiopulmonary function, contributing to sleep fragmentation and sleepiness. Nicotine also alters sleep architecture.

cat__smkstat5_3.0.label: Plausible
cat__smkstat5_3.0.reason: Smoking status can affect sleep continuity and respiratory physiology, increasing risk of sleep-disordered breathing and nonrestorative sleep. These pathways plausibly increase daytime sleepiness.

cat__types5_5.0.label: Needs caution
cat__types5_5.0.reason: Unclear categorical type; it may encode sleep complaints, diagnoses, or treatment that correlate with sleepiness. Potential for confounding or partial construct overlap depending on definition.

cat__wrksched5_7.0.label: Plausible
cat__wrksched5_7.0.reason: Irregular or nonstandard work schedules can cause circadian misalignment and chronic sleep restriction. Both are strong causal drivers of excessive daytime sleepiness.

num__AHI.label: Plausible
num__AHI.reason: Apnea-hypopnea index measures sleep apnea severity, which causes arousals and intermittent hypoxia. These mechanisms commonly lead to excessive daytime sleepiness.

num__ArousalIndex.label: Plausible
num__ArousalIndex.reason: Frequent arousals fragment sleep and reduce restorative sleep depth. Sleep fragmentation is a direct cause of daytime sleepiness.

num__AwakeningIndex.label: Plausible
num__AwakeningIndex.reason: More awakenings indicate poorer sleep continuity and greater fragmentation. Fragmented sleep increases daytime sleepiness via reduced restorative sleep.

num__N1_pct.label: Plausible
num__N1_pct.reason: Higher N1 proportion often reflects lighter, more fragmented sleep and can be elevated in OSA or insomnia. Lighter sleep is associated with nonrestorative sleep and sleepiness.

num__N2_pct.label: Plausible
num__N2_pct.reason: Changes in N2 proportion can reflect altered sleep architecture and fragmentation. While less specific, architecture shifts can plausibly relate to restorative quality and sleepiness.

num__N3_pct.label: Plausible
num__N3_pct.reason: N3 (slow-wave sleep) supports restorative processes; reduced N3 can lead to nonrestorative sleep and increased sleepiness. It can also be reduced by fragmentation and aging.

num__ObstructiveApneaIndex.label: Plausible
num__ObstructiveApneaIndex.reason: Obstructive apneas cause intermittent hypoxia and arousals, degrading sleep quality. This is a well-established pathway to excessive daytime sleepiness.

num__SDNN_ms.label: Plausible
num__SDNN_ms.reason: SDNN reflects overall HRV and autonomic balance; reduced HRV can indicate stress, arousals, or cardiopulmonary disease affecting sleep quality. These factors can contribute to daytime sleepiness.

num__SOL_min.label: Plausible
num__SOL_min.reason: Longer sleep onset latency can indicate insomnia or hyperarousal, reducing effective sleep and increasing fatigue/sleepiness. It can also reflect circadian misalignment.

num__SWA_Decline_Ratio.label: Plausible
num__SWA_Decline_Ratio.reason: The decline of slow-wave activity across the night indexes homeostatic sleep pressure dissipation. Abnormal decline can indicate disrupted restorative sleep, plausibly increasing daytime sleepiness.

num__SWA_Early.label: Plausible
num__SWA_Early.reason: Early-night SWA reflects accumulated sleep pressure and restorative deep sleep intensity. Reduced early SWA can signal impaired restorative sleep and contribute to daytime sleepiness.
